intro: If you're hunting for a place to stay in the Na Pa-Mueang Chon Buri area that isn't a hotel block with rooms lined up wall to wall, but instead a "standalone bungalow room set in a garden, quiet, with private parking right outside your room, at a price you can actually afford," Patoey House is a name worth keeping on your list · it's a 2.5-star bungalow-style guest house at 47/11 Moo 11, Tambon Na Pa, Mueang Chon Buri · what guests bring up most often is that the rooms are clean, the setting is quiet and shady, the beds are comfy, and there's private parking right outside the room with no jostling for a spot — which suits people driving themselves, industrial-estate workers who want somewhere quiet, travellers stopping over mid-journey, and families who'd rather have privacy than a room inside a block · it's also pet-friendly, which isn't common at this price · it sits about 8.3 km from Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, near the temples and markets in the Na Pa area · prices start at around THB 490/night · scored 8.7 from 5 reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who Patoey House is for, in a nutshell — if I had to sum it up in one line, Patoey House is a budget bungalow-style guest house for people who want "a quiet, private room with parking right outside" in the Na Pa area of Mueang Chon Buri, rather than the feel of a big hotel or a sea view · it's not a beachfront resort where you step out of your room onto the sand, there's no pool, and it doesn't lean on luxury facilities · what it is is a standalone-bungalow stay set in a garden, designed for comfortable, private rest — whether you're staying a single night mid-journey or several days at a stretch · real reviews line up on who this place suits: people working at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and the surrounding area who want somewhere quiet, people driving themselves who want private parking right outside the room, travellers stopping over on the route from Bangkok to Pattaya or the eastern provinces, and families who'd rather have privacy than a room in a block of rooms side by side · another group that says they were impressed is people who brought a pet, because it's pet-friendly — something that's hard to find at the same price · put simply, Patoey House plays on "quiet, calm and private" on a light budget for a stay in Chon Buri, while still keeping things clean, which is exactly where guests rate it highest

Location and getting around — Patoey House is at 47/11 Moo 11, Tambon Na Pa, Mueang Chon Buri · the thing to understand before you book is that it's not right on the beach and not in the centre of Chon Buri town, but in the Na Pa area, a semi-residential, semi-industrial zone, on the quieter, shadier inner side · the location advantage that works in its favour is that it's about 8.3 km from Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, a short drive away, which suits people coming to work, run errands or attend meetings at the estate and wanting somewhere quiet, away from the bustle · within a short drive of the property there are several points of interest, such as Wat Rat Samoson about 0.6 km away, Wat Thong Khung about 2 km, and Amata Castle about 2.4 km · within a few kilometres there are dozens of restaurants and shopping spots like Tubtim Siam (Tukcom), plus a fish market in the area · for people from Bangkok, it sits in a handy stopover position on the route to Pattaya and the eastern provinces, about 40-something km from Suvarnabhumi Airport · the straightforward observation is that it suits people with a car more than people without one, because it's in an area where public transport isn't very convenient — without your own car you'll mainly rely on ride-hailing apps or hired cars, which in the Na Pa area may not come as readily as in the town centre or around Bang Saen beach

"Clean room, really quiet, slept well, parked right outside the room without walking far, shady setting like staying at a garden house, great for people coming to work near the estate who want somewhere quiet, and the price is really light too."

Room types and decor — Patoey House is a bungalow-style stay that splits its rooms into several tiers to choose from by budget and number of people · it starts with the Single Room, which has an en-suite bathroom and suits solo travellers or workers on a short stay · stepping up there's the Standard Queen for couples or anyone wanting a bigger bed, the Deluxe King, which is more spacious and a bit more polished in its decor, and a twin room with 5-foot beds that suits families or groups of friends travelling together · the defining feature here is that the rooms are standalone bungalows set within a garden, which feels more private than rooms inside a block lined up together, and many rooms have parking right outside the door · the decor leans toward simple, warm, home-like tones rather than anything flashy, but it looks clean and tidy · most real reviews agree in their praise that the rooms are very clean, the beds are comfy, and the quiet setting makes for good sleep — the three things nightly-stay guests weigh most, in line with a cleanliness score as high as 9.3 out of 10 on Trip.com · one observation that comes up is that, since this is a small guest-house-style stay, the in-room amenities may not be as complete as a full hotel, so it's worth checking the exact in-room items you want when you book, especially if you're coming as a group or staying several days

Facilities (no pool, but enough for a quiet stay) — let's be straight from the start: Patoey House has no pool and no gym, because it's a bungalow-style guest house rather than a resort or a big hotel · but for an actual stay in the Na Pa area, it has the essentials in the right measure · the highlight guests praise most is the private parking right outside the room and free parking on the grounds, which many reviews agree is easy with no jostling for a spot — the main reason people driving themselves choose this place · another thing that draws praise is the shady, quiet garden setting, which makes it feel more like a holiday house than a hotel in town · it's also pet-friendly, which is hard to find at the same price, and suits people who don't want to leave the dog or cat at home · on top of that there's free Wi-Fi, CCTV in the common areas, an alarm system, a separate smoking area, and a restaurant on the grounds · so the strength here isn't "resort toys" but privacy and the quiet calm of a garden house, which fits industrial-estate workers and stopover travellers more squarely than a pool they might not even use

Food and places nearby — Patoey House has a restaurant on the grounds, but no breakfast service, and it's not a place you come to mainly to eat on-site · most reviews don't dwell on a hotel-style buffet breakfast, so set your expectations that meals will mainly rely on the spots around you, which is normal for a budget guest-house-style stay · the upside is that the Na Pa location has made-to-order eateries, rice shops and convenience stores within a short drive, and area listings note dozens of restaurants within a few kilometres · if you want serious Chon Buri specialities, you can drive out to the town centre or markets in the area where there's seafood and local treats to choose from · for industrial-estate workers who head out for dinner and come back to sleep, having a convenience store nearby and parking right outside the room makes it easy to grab something to eat back in the room · overall, food at Patoey House is more about "easy to rely on the places around you" than a selling point of the stay itself · another thing worth knowing is that some payments are cash only as stated, so it's worth carrying a bit of cash for convenience

Service and care — service at Patoey House is broadly in the range guests are happy with, fitting for a budget guest house · real reviews mostly speak positively about the cleanliness of the rooms and the quiet, and praise the staff as helpful and friendly · the point worth saying straight is that this is a small stay where the reception desk is open during set hours with limited staff, generally from around 9:00 AM to midnight, and at some times you may need to contact the property in advance to arrange a check-in time · so if you're arriving late or outside reception hours, you should give a clear heads-up on your check-in time so the property can be ready in time · this is normal for a small bungalow-style stay that doesn't have staff on duty 24 hours like a big hotel, and it usually isn't a problem if you communicate clearly from the time you book · overall, if you set your expectations correctly — a clean, quiet, budget guest house rather than a full-service hotel — most experiences come out well

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com and other booking platforms, the picture that emerges is fairly consistent · On the praise side: very clean rooms (a cleanliness score as high as 9.3 out of 10), a quiet, shady garden-house setting, comfy beds, private parking right outside the room with no jostling, the privacy of standalone bungalows, pet-friendly, budget-friendly value, and a handy location for people working at Amata Nakorn · On the gripes side: what comes up is a smell from the bathroom drain in some rooms, which some people fix by closing the bathroom door when it's not in use, the fact that the desk has limited staff and is open during set hours, meaning you need to arrange your check-in time in advance, the fact that there's no pool and no breakfast for those expecting a hotel feel, and the fact that it's not right on the beach or in the town centre, so you have to drive out to get around · these gripes are mostly about setting your expectations correctly (a bungalow guest house, not a hotel or resort) and communicating clearly with the property before booking, rather than being big problems · one extra thing to know is that this is a new place that still doesn't have many reviews (around 5 on Trip.com), so the average score is based on a small sample, and it's worth reading the latest reviews before deciding

"Overall better than the price suggests — clean room, quiet, easy parking right outside the room · one tiny gripe was a smell from the bathroom drain at first, but closing the bathroom door sorted it; giving a heads-up on your check-in time makes it smoother. Great for people driving themselves who want somewhere quiet around Chon Buri."

Price and value — Patoey House clearly sits in Chon Buri's budget tier · nightly rates start at around THB 490/night for a queen room in normal periods, rising by room type (Deluxe King / twin room) and on holidays, generally still in the few-hundred to low-thousand-per-night range · what makes it good value is that you get the privacy of a standalone bungalow with parking right outside the room at a lighter price than a hotel in a block, a combination that isn't common in this budget · compared with stays in the Chon Buri town area and near the estate at the same level, where Patoey House comes out ahead is on quiet, the cleanliness guests rate highly, and being pet-friendly · but you trade that for no pool, no breakfast, no beachfront, and a desk that isn't open 24 hours · if the goal of your stay is "sleep clean, quiet, cheap, with parking right outside the room, and use it as a base for work or a stopover in Chon Buri," every baht you spend at Patoey House comes back as good value · but if the goal is a seaside resort feel or the full set of facilities of a big hotel, the lower price comes with limits you'll have to accept

What to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, if you're arriving late or outside the desk's hours (generally around 9:00 AM to midnight), give a heads-up on your check-in time directly with the property to arrange the handover · Two, there's no pool, no breakfast, and no beachfront, so if you want to hit the sea or want a resort feel, allow time to drive out · Three, some payments are cash only as stated, so carry some cash · Four, it suits people with a car more, because it's in the Na Pa area where public transport isn't convenient — without a car, budget for ride-hailing to get around the area · Five, if you're bringing a pet, let them know and ask about the pet policy with the property clearly before booking · Six, since it's a new place that still doesn't have many reviews, it's worth reading the latest reviews and choosing a free-cancellation option first if your plans aren't firm, while comparing prices across platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com)

Summary — from all the real reviews, Patoey House is the best fit for people working at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and the surrounding area who want somewhere quiet, people driving themselves who want private parking right outside the room, travellers stopping over mid-journey, and families who want the privacy of a bungalow at a light price · the strengths guests bring up consistently are clean rooms, a quiet, shady garden-house setting, comfy beds, parking right outside the room, and being pet-friendly — which makes it a good base for people using Chon Buri for work or as a place to pass through · but you have to accept, honestly, that there's no pool, no breakfast, no beachfront, the desk is open during set hours, and you should give a heads-up on your check-in time and carry some cash · if you're looking for a seaside resort where you step out of your room onto the sand, or a hotel with a pool and full service, this may not be the answer, and you should consider stays around Bang Saen beach or Pattaya instead · but for a budget stay in Chon Buri, easy driving, and wanting a clean, quiet, private room like staying at a garden house — Patoey House is an option that meets that need at good value, on a budget you can actually afford
